Subject: RFP: contract questionnaire — IP, liability & export controls

Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick engagement on the RFP. Attached is Lumina's standard questionnaire — we're primarily looking for firm positions on: IP ownership for model outputs and embeddings, indemnity scope (esp. third-party IP), financial liability caps, and how Redwood handles export controls (ECCN/dual-use concerns). We have an order form template attached to the RFP as well and would like to confirm whether Redwood's standard commercial order form aligns with the terms you're providing in the questionnaire.

Two quick asks up front:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will 1) accept an assignment of deliverable IP, or alternatively provide an exclusive or perpetual license in the order form?
- What is your standard liability cap and does it differ for security incidents vs. IP infringement?

We'd appreciate completed answers inline in the attached spreadsheet and a short call later today if possible.

Regards,
David Chen
Director, Procurement
Lumina Systems

David — thanks for sending and for the clear priorities. I've attached a completed copy of the questionnaire with Redwood's responses (high level) and a draft order form for your procurement team to review. Looping in Laura from Legal and Aditya (SE) for specific IP wording and export-control tech detail.

Quick summary to save time:
- IP: Customer retains ownership of its data and inputs. For model outputs, Redwood grants customers a broad, royalty-free license to use outputs for their business purposes. Redwood retains ownership of models and model weights. We do not accept blanket assignment of Redwood model IP, but we can discuss narrow, deliverable-specific license language in the order form.
- Indemnity: Redwood's standard indemnity covers third-party IP infringement claims directly related to our services; customers are expected to indemnify for content they provide that causes harm.
- Liability cap: Our commercial position ties aggregate liability to fees paid (12-month lookback), with carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
- Export controls: Redwood complies with US export regulations; we do not export to sanctioned parties/regions and will work with customers to identify ECCN/licensing needs.

I've attached: Lumina_RFP_QA_completed.xlsx (our completed answers), Draft_Order_Form_v3.pdf (commercial terms). Laura — please see section-by-section legal responses below and advise if we need changes before we send back to Lumina. Aditya — any tech notes on ECCN/data residency you want to add?

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: RFP: contract questionnaire — IP, liability & export controls (detailed responses)

David / Jonas — attaching formal legal responses below mapped to Lumina's questionnaire sections. Where Lumina asks for redlines we flag flexibility and what we consider non-starters. Happy to hop on a call to walk through.

1) IP ownership and deliverables- Redwood position: Customers retain all right, title and interest in Customer Data (defined as all data and content provided by Customer). Redwood does not claim ownership of Customer Data.
- Model outputs ("Deliverables"): Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, and display Deliverables for Customer's internal business purposes and to provide products/services to Customer's customers. If Lumina requires assignment of Deliverables, we can discuss assignment for narrow, bespoke deliverables produced under the SOW, subject to additional consideration and explicit language in the order form.

2) Model IP and improvements- Redwood retains ownership of models, model weights, training procedures, and general improvements to the platform. We will not be required to assign model IP or underlying improvements. For customers wanting exclusivity on a specific fine-tuned model, we will evaluate on a case-by-case commercial basis.

3) Indemnity- Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services, as delivered by Redwood, infringe a third party's U.S. intellectual property rights, provided that Customer: (a) gives Redwood prompt written notice; (b) allows Redwood to control the defense and settlement; and (c) provides reasonable cooperation. Redwood's obligation does not extend to claims arising from Customer Data, Customer modifications, or Customer's use outside the scope of the Agreement.

4) Liability cap and carve-outs- Aggregate liability: Except for liability arising from (i) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) Redwood's breach of its confidentiality obligations, and (iii) amounts payable under Redwood's indemnity for IP infringement, Redwood's aggregate liability to Customer will be limited to the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable order form during the preceding twelve (12) months, or (b) $100,000.
- Security incidents: We treat security incidents seriously; for breach-related claims we agree that the foregoing liability cap applies except where local law mandates higher recoveries.

5) Warranties & disclaimers- Redwood provides a limited warranty that the Services will materially conform to the Documentation. Except as expressly set forth, Services are provided "as is" and Redwood disclaims other warranties to the extent permitted by law.

6) Export controls and ECCN- Redwood complies with U.S. export laws and will not knowingly provide Services to embargoed or sanctioned entities/regions. Customers must not use the Services to transfer controlled technical data to prohibited end users. If Lumina believes that specific content or deliverables may require an export license (e.g., dual-use ECCN classification), notify us and we will engage our compliance team. For certain restricted jurisdictions, we may require export licenses or contractually restrict use.

7) Data processing and residency- Redwood will process Customer Data in accordance with the Data Processing Addendum (DPA). By default, data processing occurs in the region(s) specified in the order form; we can offer region-specific deployments for customers with residency requirements (subject to Dedicated/Private deployment terms and minimum commitments).

8) Order form / commercial terms- Draft_Order_Form_v3.pdf contains our standard payment and termination terms. We can accommodate a limited set of procurement redlines (e.g., PO-based invoicing, standard insurance updates). Material changes to the liability/indemnity/IP sections will require escalation to Legal and may affect pricing/commitments.

9) SOC 2 / evidence- Per your request, attached is a Redwood SOC 2 summary and an outline of available audit artifacts. Full SOC 2 reports can be provided under NDA.

If Lumina would like a tighter liability floor or assignment of deliverables we will need to move to a commercial exception with associated pricing and approval.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / Jonas — thanks for the thorough responses and the attachments. A few follow-ups:

1) Assignment of Deliverables: Lumina's legal team will likely press for assignment/perpetual exclusivity on a small set of regulatory report templates produced as Deliverables. You note assignment is possible for bespoke deliverables — can you flag the commercial owner we should speak with if we need an exception?

2) Liability floor: Lumina prefers a liability floor rather than a low $100k fallback. Would Redwood consider a negotiated floor tied to subscription tier? If not, we may propose a higher minimum.

3) Data residency redline: we will propose language that requires processing to occur in the US-East region for the first 24 months. Can you confirm whether the Dedicated/Private deployment options would be required to meet that guarantee?

4) SOC2 report: we'll take the NDA route and request the full report.

Let's schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow 10am PT to finalize any open commercial exceptions — Jonas, can you coordinate?

Best,
David
Director, Procurement
Lumina Systems
